scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: An X-ray can see your bones through skin and muscle. How does light pass right through you?

scenes.name: energy
scenes.text: X-rays are a kind of light, but with far more energy than the light our eyes can see.

scenes.name: pass
scenes.text: They pass easily through soft tissue like skin, fat and muscle.

scenes.name: absorb
scenes.text: Bones contain calcium, which absorbs much more X-ray energy, so fewer rays get through.

scenes.name: shadow
scenes.text: A detector behind you records what gets through. Bones show up white, like shadows, and soft areas look dark.

scenes.name: ct
scenes.text: A CT scanner takes many X-rays from different angles, and a computer builds slices of your body.

scenes.name: safety
scenes.text: X-rays are ionising, so doses are kept low, and that's why you see lead aprons and warning signs.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Pass through, absorb, shadow. Follow for more on how things really work.
